body.statement:
Let \(p_n(0)=p_0\), put \(m=|\mathcal J|\), and fix a compact \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) that is eventually contained in \(\mathcal U_n\) and in one completed positive-support stratum.  Fix a Gaussian rule for \(\mathfrak G_0\) whose finite representation has Gaussian-null boundaries.  Define
\[
d_n(C)=\sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}-Bu\right\|_2,
\qquad
\delta_n(C)=\max_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|,
\]
where the maximum is zero if \(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}=\varnothing\), and put
\[
x_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C),
\qquad
A_0=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}},
\]
with an empty sum equal to zero.  There is a parameter-independent Carter transfer producing \(K_n\) such that every semantic coverage probability and every normalized diameter-risk expectation on \(C\) differs from its Gaussian counterpart by at most
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal E}_n(C)=
C_{2/\kappa}\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}
+(H_C+A_0)x_n(C)+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C).
\]
Here \(H_C<\infty\) is obtained by finite rational active-set enumeration and \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\) is the explicit Hellinger upper bound between the score-normal law and \(N_d(u,\Sigma_0)\).  Each term tends to zero, so \(\widetilde{\mathcal E}_n(C)\to0\).  This conclusion does not assert an \(O(n^{-1/2})\) total rate unless rates for \(x_n(C)\) and \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\) are separately supplied.
body.justification: The revised theorem gives the first complete Carter-backed compact comparison receipt.
body.gap: Its new proof separates Carter's total-variation term from score covariance and semantic arrangement stability.
body.consumer: Job Corps cell counts inherit compact coverage and diameter-risk guarantees.
body.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: parameter-independent Le Cam transfer, an explicit Gaussian Hellinger calculation, and finite-arrangement stability.}

Write \(D_n=\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}\), \(I_n=B'D_n^{-1}B\), and \(\Sigma_n=I_n^{-1}\).  By \(\text{prop:carter-fixed-m-positive-cell}\), uniformly over \(u\in C\), all multinomial coordinates are eventually at least \(\kappa/2\), their largest-to-smallest ratio is at most \(2/\kappa\), and Carter's parameter-independent kernel has total-variation error
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car},n}
=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
For a matched normal vector \(Y_n\), apply the parameter-independent affine score map
\[
S_n(Y_n)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}\frac{Y_n-np_n(0)}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Its law at \(p_n(u)\) is \(N_d\{\mu_n(u),V_n(u)\}\), where
\[
\mu_n(u)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\},                         \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
V_n(u)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}
\left[\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(u)\}-p_n(u)p_n(u)'\right]
D_n^{-1}B\Sigma_n.                                                            \tag{3}
\]
Because \(\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}B=I_d\), (2) gives
\[
\sup_{u\in C}\|\mu_n(u)-u\|_2
\leq \|\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}d_n(C)\longrightarrow0.           \tag{4}
\]
The last convergence uses \(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\), while eventual boundedness of the matrix norm follows from \(\text{ass:multinomial-base-convergence}\), \(\text{ass:multinomial-interior}\), the full column rank of \(B\), and \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\).  Equations (3)--(4), the same lemma, and compactness of \(C\) imply
\[
\sup_{u\in C}\|V_n(u)-\Sigma_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow0.            \tag{5}
\]

For positive definite \(V\), direct completion of squares in the integral of the square root of the two Gaussian densities gives
\[
\mathsf H^2(\mu,V;u,\Sigma_0)
=2-2\frac{|V|^{1/4}|\Sigma_0|^{1/4}}
{|(V+\Sigma_0)/2|^{1/2}}
\exp\left[-\frac18(\mu-u)'\{(V+\Sigma_0)/2\}^{-1}(\mu-u)\right].          \tag{6}
\]
The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality applied to the positive and negative parts of the density difference yields total variation at most \(\min\{1,\mathsf H\}\).  Define
\[
\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
=\sup_{u\in C}\min\{1,\mathsf H(\mu_n(u),V_n(u);u,\Sigma_0)\}.              \tag{7}
\]
Uniform positive definiteness following from (5), together with (4)--(6), proves
\[
\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\longrightarrow0.                            \tag{8}
\]

The exact moving-slack identity in \(\text{def:moving-slack-system}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\) give a finite active-set constant \(H_C\) such that every finite-sample semantic label at \(u\in C\) is an incident Gaussian label at a point displaced by at most \(H_Cx_n(C)\) in \(\Sigma_0^{-1}\)-norm.  The same enumeration applies to each rival semantic union and to each active projection system defining the separated domain; enlarging \(H_C\) by the maximum of the finitely many inverse-basis norms charges the corresponding risk-set restoration.  Equalities lose no label because every equality face belongs to all incident completions.  Translation of equal-covariance Gaussian laws by Mahalanobis distance \(t\) has total variation \(2\Phi(t/2)-1\leq t/\sqrt{2\pi}\), so its numerical factor may also be absorbed into this finite \(H_C\).

Set the protected-band width equal to \(\tau=x_n(C)\).  The indicator \(\mathbf1\{x_n(C)>\tau\}\) is then zero.  Since every \(a_j\ne0\) and \(\Sigma_0\succ0\), each denominator below is positive, and the definition of \(\mathfrak b_0\) gives, for every \(x\geq0\),
\[
\mathfrak b_0(x)
=\sum_j\min\left\{1,
\frac{2x}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}\right\}
\leq A_0x.                                                                     \tag{9}
\]
Thus the complete semantic contribution is at most
\[
H_Cx_n(C)+\mathfrak b_0\{x_n(C)\}
\leq(H_C+A_0)x_n(C).                                                           \tag{10}
\]
Finally, apply \(\text{lem:bounded-semantic-transfer-by-tv}\) to the Carter kernel, to the score-normal covariance replacement, and to the Gaussian translations used in (10).  Coverage indicators take values in \([0,1]\), and \(0\leq\ell_0\leq1\), so (1), (7), and (10) add without a loss-scale multiplier and yield exactly \(\widetilde{\mathcal E}_n(C)\).  The convergence \(d_n(C)\to0\) is \(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\), the convergence \(\delta_n(C)\to0\) is \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\), and (8) handles covariance replacement.  Hence \(\widetilde{\mathcal E}_n(C)\to0\).  Because neither cited premise supplies a rate for the last three quantities, no overall \(O(n^{-1/2})\) assertion follows.
